skill.name: hyperframes-keyframes
skill.description: Guides seek-safe HyperFrames keyframes for GSAP, CSS, Anime.js, WAAPI, SVG, text, and 3D motion with focused diagnostics.
skill.summary: Author deterministic HyperFrames keyframes and verify motion with focused diagnostics.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around API names, options, and examples. The skill does contain legitimate HyperFrames CLI diagnostic instructions, including npx commands, so external command use should require user confirmation.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to run HyperFrames CLI diagnostics, including npx-based commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running CLI diagnostics, and prefer a local or pinned HyperFrames CLI installation.

remediation.issue: Selector, file, time, and angle placeholders may become shell arguments during diagnostics.
remediation.suggestion: Document that agents must quote user-supplied values or pass them as argv arguments instead of concatenating shell strings.

content.value_statement: HyperFrames animations can fail when timelines are not seek-safe or proof frames are unclear. This skill guides deterministic keyframes and focused verification.
actual_capabilities: Defines seek-safe runtime rules for GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, and WAAPI.
Guides mechanism choices for FLIP, paths, masks, SVG draw, SVG morph, text motion, and 3D depth.
Names animated subjects, required poses, final states, and proof times for HyperFrames compositions.
Provides CLI verification steps for keyframe diagnostics, focused shots, ghost views, and snapshots.
Troubleshoots endpoint-only motion, identity breaks, fake 3D, wrong finals, and unreadable text.
limitations: Requires an existing HyperFrames composition or starter scene.
Does not provide broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning.
Does not replace manual review of rendered proof frames.
CLI diagnostics may require shell access and user approval.

use_cases.title: Make motion deterministic
use_cases.description: Convert animation ideas into seek-safe poses, final states, and runtime registration rules.

use_cases.title: Verify a HyperFrames scene
use_cases.description: Plan focused diagnostics that prove target motion, route shape, readable text, and final lockup.

use_cases.title: Choose the right mechanism
use_cases.description: Select FLIP, path travel, masks, SVG draw, text subdivision, or 3D camera motion for a specific brief.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Keyframes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single animated subject.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $hyperframes-keyframes to create a seek-safe keyframe plan for this HyperFrames scene. Identify the subject, poses, final state, and proof checks.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Unreliable Motion
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a scene that does not scrub correctly.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $hyperframes-keyframes to review this animation for autoplay, timers, random values, missing holds, and unregistered runtimes. Explain the fixes before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Mechanism
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with several possible animation methods.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $hyperframes-keyframes to compare path travel, FLIP, masks, SVG draw, text subdivision, and 3D depth for this motion brief. Choose the smallest mechanism.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Proof Results
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request after diagnostics or snapshots are available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $hyperframes-keyframes to interpret my keyframe, shot, ghost, and snapshot results. Find the failing proof times and the source changes needed.

output_examples.input: A card must move from one dashboard panel to another without looking like a fade replacement.
output_examples.output: The response names the card as the persistent subject, recommends FLIP or one continuous transform, sets source and target poses, and asks for focused proof frames.

output_examples.input: A WebGL product scene should show real depth while the camera moves around the object.
output_examples.output: The response defines camera, target, object, material, and ghost-view checks so the rendered pixels prove depth instead of simple scale.

output_examples.input: Text wave animation is hard to read after the first second.
output_examples.output: The response preserves line boxes, reduces displacement, adds readable holds, and requests snapshots at the text proof times and final state.

best_practices: Name the animated subject, visible poses, final state, and proof times before editing.
Use deterministic runtime construction with finite durations and registered timelines or instances.
Verify the smallest failing diagnostic before rendering the full composition again.
anti_patterns: Do not use timers, unseeded random values, hover triggers, or autoplay for render-critical motion.
Do not replace a moving subject with a crossfade when continuity must be visible.
Do not treat logs or helper overlays as proof when full-frame pixels show a broken result.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create deterministic 2D and 3D keyframes for HyperFrames compositions.

faq.question: Which animation runtimes does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, SVG techniques, DOM 3D, Three.js, and WebGL patterns.

faq.question: Can it design an entire video concept?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on keyframes, runtime behavior, mechanism choice, and proof diagnostics for an existing composition.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill recommends HyperFrames CLI diagnostics, but users should approve command execution before an agent runs them.

faq.question: How does it verify motion quality?
faq.answer: It uses focused shots, ghost views, snapshots, and final-frame checks to confirm visible motion and stable endings.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it for media sourcing, captions, brand strategy, broad story planning, or non-HyperFrames animation work.
